CORRECTED_BY_A_SECOND_INDEPENDENT_REFERE.the_hypothesis_this_points_at: the QUANTIZE/DEQUANTIZE pair on the layer-2 KV. The vendor quantises the whole post-RoPE vector in place; its measured QDQ delta is 0.0 at layer 0 and 0.125 at a later layer, so a device QDQ with the wrong block geometry or scale format would be INVISIBLE at layer 0 and visible as a few per cent at layer 2 -- which is exactly the observed pattern of exact layers 0 and 1 and a few-per-cent layer 2.
what_follows: the reference is now corroborated by two mutually independent computations, so the divergence is on the device or graph side
path matching is MOOT -- there is nothing to match, because the two paths already agree -- and the front-end variant I costed last commit is unnecessary

there IS a fault to find, and the aligned layer-2 measurement is evidence of it rather than of accumulated rounding: the window rows differ by about five per cent while the residual entering layer 2 is 0.99935 correct, and a projection of an almost-exact input cannot be five per cent wrong by accumulation
CORRECTED_BY_A_SECOND_INDEPENDENT_REFERE.what_was_concluded: that the device's divergence is a genuine numeric-path difference -- device MXFP4 against reference FP8-recast -- and that closing the cell needs path matching or full scale rather than a bug hunt.
CORRECTED_BY_A_SECOND_INDEPENDENT_REFERE.why: a second reference on the SHIPPED fp4 path -- the same FP4 codes and E8M0 scales, the same activation quantisation, one PyTorch dequantisation in place of the broken kernel, which is the other of the two independent references runtime/reference/deepseek_v4_oracle.py names -- produces IDENTICAL logits to the FP8 recast: argmax 3118, top1 0.97164, top2 1946 at 0.798973, margin 0.172667, and the same 16-token sequence. The expert numeric path therefore does not move the output at this scale, so it cannot be what separates the device from the reference.

FEASIBILITY_OF_PATH_MATCHING.and_there_is_a_fidelity_cost: the shipped DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash declares expert_dtype fp4. An FP8-expert deployment is therefore a VARIANT of the product, not the product. It would make the reduced comparison exact and it would be validating a variant's numerics -- worth doing deliberately and worth not doing by accident, which is why this is recorded rather than started.
FEASIBILITY_OF_PATH_MATCHING.checked: compiler/frontends/v3/deepseek_v41.py line 4475 starts the routed expert as MXFP4_SWIGLU unconditionally, and the routed expert's weight declarations (lines ~3563 and ~3705) name dtype mxfp4_e2m1 directly. FP8_SWIGLU exists in the same front end but is used only for the one shared expert every token runs.
FEASIBILITY_OF_PATH_MATCHING.the_honest_position: the three V4.1 cells are blocked on this vehicle. Everything reachable without changing what is being built has been done: the reference is now sound (its predecessor's routed experts were dead), the fixture no longer saturates its own clamp, layers 0 and 1 agree to five decimals, the compressor's index path is bit-exact, and the residual divergence is a few per cent per layer of genuine numeric-path difference. Closing them needs either a front-end variant or a shipped-scale run, and both are decisions about scope rather than debugging.
FEASIBILITY_OF_PATH_MATCHING.therefore: putting both sides on the FP8 expert path is a FRONT-END change, not a fixture flag: the routed expert's operator kind, its weight dtypes and its block geometry all have to become conditional on the declared expert dtype. That is tractable and it is not a quick edit.

answer: it is material. A tolerance-based comparison does NOT close this cell.
not_a_claim: not an RTL measurement: the device is runtime.sim
r = 0.48 does not say which side is right. It says they differ, and the reference is the external comparator by construction.
this is the reduced vehicle. It says nothing about the shipped V4.1 model, whose cells have never been run.
question: the device and the corrected reference differ by a few per cent per layer; does a tolerance-based comparison close the cell, or is the accumulated difference material?
reading: r = 0.48 is not the signature of two implementations that agree numerically and disagree only at the argmax. The output distributions genuinely differ, which is what a few-per-cent divergence per layer compounds to over forty layers.
the reference's own argmax is reasonably decisive -- margin 0.173 with only two logits inside it -- so the disagreement is not the reference being ill-conditioned the way the v1 fixture was.
the DEVICE's top-1 margin is 0.00515, essentially a tie, so its argmax is the part that is fragile. That is a property of this reduced vehicle's distribution, not of the implementation.
what_closing_this_cell_would_require: path matching: build the deployment and the oracle on the SAME routed-expert and KV numeric path. The device computes MXFP4 under the contracts it was admitted against; the reference computes the vendor's FP8 recast. Both are legitimate and they are not the same arithmetic, and at reduced scale the difference compounds. A fixture and an IR declaring fp8 experts -- the release README's own documented alternative, which the shared expert already uses -- would put both sides on one path.

or full scale: all three DeepSeek-V4-Flash cells match an FP8-expert oracle from an MXFP4 device at shipped scale, where trained weights keep magnitudes small and the per-layer difference does not compound the same way. A shipped V4.1 token costs days of simulation at the measured rate, which is why the reduced vehicle exists.
what it does NOT require is another bug hunt at layer 2: six hypotheses are closed there and the aligned measurement shows a few per cent, not a fault.
